title: What can be done if a baby is likely to be born too early
intro: A baby born before thirty-seven weeks of pregnancy is considered premature. When there are signs of early labour, doctors can sometimes delay birth for a short time and give treatments that improve the baby's chance of doing well. Understanding the options helps parents take part in decisions.

sections.heading: Signs and risk factors
paragraphs: Warning signs include regular contractions, lower abdominal or back pain, pressure in the pelvis, a change in vaginal discharge, bleeding or fluid leaking from the vagina. Risk factors include a previous premature birth, a short cervix, multiple pregnancy, infections, smoking, certain medical conditions and uterine abnormalities. If you notice signs, contact your midwife or hospital immediately.

sections.heading: Assessment
paragraphs: Doctors examine you, check the baby with a heart tracing and ultrasound, may measure cervical length, and test for fetal fibronectin or infection. They look at the length of pregnancy and the baby's position. Tests help judge whether labour is likely to start in the next days.

sections.heading: Treatments to improve outcomes
paragraphs: Corticosteroid injections given to the mother mature the baby's lungs and reduce breathing problems, brain bleeds and death, and are most helpful when birth is expected within seven days, in pregnancy up to about thirty-four weeks. Magnesium sulphate given before very early birth protects the baby's brain. Antibiotics are given when waters have broken or infection is suspected.

sections.heading: Delaying birth and moving to a specialist unit
paragraphs: Medicines called tocolytics can slow contractions for about two days, which gives time for steroids to work and to transfer the mother to a hospital with a neonatal intensive care unit. Bed rest has not been shown to help. For women with a short cervix or earlier premature birth, progesterone, a stitch in the cervix or a pessary may reduce the risk in selected cases.

sections.heading: After birth and support
paragraphs: Premature babies may need help with breathing, warmth and feeding in a neonatal unit. Parents are encouraged to take part, with skin-to-skin contact and breast milk. Outcomes depend on gestational age at birth, and follow-up checks monitor development. Emotional support, counselling and parent groups help families cope.

examples.title: Acting on warning signs
examples.text: Imagine you feel regular tightening at thirty weeks. You could call your maternity unit right away and go in for assessment.

examples.title: Preparing for the unit
examples.text: Suppose a transfer is advised. You might ask what treatments are planned, who can accompany you and how to stay in touch with family.
